author: TEDx Talks
description: Why women’s exhaustion and anxiety can have an overlooked biological dimension, and why building products around women’s biology starts with asking better questions and measuring what we too often miss - including something as fundamental as iron deficiency. Dominika is a scientist and founder working at the intersection of women’s health, biology and data. As founder and CEO of The Iron Bar, she is confronting one of women’s most normalised health crises: iron deficiency. Her talk will explore how the problem became so widely accepted and what building a better solution actually takes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: It’s Not in Your Head - It’s in Your Blood | Dr. Dominika Repcikova | TEDxCoolhaven Women

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if protecting someone from getting hurt also prevents them from finding love? Adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities deserve the same opportunities for connection, romance, and meaningful relationships as anyone else. Yet fear of exploitation often leads families, caregivers, and communities to avoid conversations about dating, consent, and intimacy altogether. Katherine Gyolai, founder of Find Love Safely and mother and stepmother to eight adult children, four with intellectual or developmental disabilities, challenges us to reconsider what protection really means. She reveals why relationship education—not avoidance—is essential to helping adults recognize healthy connections, establish boundaries, make informed choices, and pursue love more safely. Her message challenges a common assumption: We don’t protect people by denying them the opportunity to love. We empower them by giving them the tools to pursue it safely. Filmed August 4, 2026, at Orchestra Hall in
title: Mom, Can I Download Tinder? | Katherine Gyolai | TEDxMinneapolis

author: TEDx Talks
description: Success is seen, but adversity is unseen. Anil Panicker shows how hard times can reveal the strength already within us, and why the voice that says “not yet” matters more than the one that says “you can’t”. Anil Panicker is an accomplished professional with an MBA in Marketing and over 30 years of extensive Corporate Leadership Experience. He wears multiple hats as an Adversity Quotient (AQ) specialist, Leadership & Faculty Development trainer, Certified Career Mentor, and Vedic Numerologist. He is also the author of the book Born to Rise – Reborn to Shine, he also shares his insights as a YouTuber, hosting a channel with over 200 leadership and life quality enhancing videos. Throughout his career, he has successfully empowered more than 4,000 professionals and mentored upwards of 300 students, guiding them to unlock their potential and effectively thrive through adversity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local commu
title: The Unheard Superpower: The Voice That Says “Not Yet” | Anil Panicker | TEDxKIT Coimbatore

author: TEDx Talks
description: Subashri Vasudevan spent her childhood trying to be the opposite of her brother, until a phone call at her lowest point turned into 30+ co-authored books together. A warm story of sibling rivalry, second chances, and why we become who we watch. Subashri is an Assistant Vice President at Bank of America Continuum India, Chennai, with over a decade of experience in software engineering, and enterprise ETL solutions. She has built large-scale data pipeline and integration solutions across banking and financial services, working extensively with Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics, SSIS, and SQL Server. A Microsoft Community Champion, Intel Innovator, and Google Women Tech Maker, she combines deep technical expertise with active community leadership. A published author of 20 books spanning Deep Learning, Software Engineering, Digital Electronics, & Computer Networking,  published by Taylor & Francis, Wiley, Alpha Science International, and Narosa, she is also a patent holder and h
title: The Sibling Story | Subashri V | TEDxKIT Coimbatore

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Machines have learnt to speak like us, but they aren’t us, so the real question is no longer “why AI” but “who is answerable?” Pallavi Narayan explores six hard questions AI forces on us, from bias and deepfakes to the hidden cost of every prompt, and makes the case for becoming intentionally human. Pallavi Narayan is a pioneering voice at the intersection of Industrial AI and Energy, with over 25 years of experience transforming how the energy sector thinks, operates, and innovates. As an Energy Industry SME and Innovation Lead at Accenture, she has been at the forefront of designing and deploying GenAI and Agentic AI powered solutions that redefine industrial operations, from asset management and water management platforms to retail operations transformation and AI powered refinery solutions. 
A cross-functional leader who has driven end to end value creation across Product Strategy, Services Delivery, Pre-Sales, Sales, and Innovation CoE, Pallavi brings a rare combination of instru
title: In an AI World, Let’s Become Intentionally Human | Pallavi Narayan | TEDxKIT Coimbatore

author: TEDx Talks
description: A safety pin, a salt-clogged health faucet and a father’s monthly chore led to an invention, and to a bigger realisation: AI took the wall, not the idea. Dr Shriram Kris Vasudevan shows how the real barriers to innovation are now just excuses, and why the idea in your head is still yours to build. Dr. Shriram K. Vasudevan is a Senior Manager at Accenture, Coimbatore, with 19+ years spanning industry and academia in AI, Deep Learning, and Cybersecurity. A prolific author and inventor, he has co-authored 54 books for Oxford University Press, Wiley, and IET, published 150+ research articles, and holds 14 granted patents. A hackathon champion with 50+ wins at Harvard, Google, AICTE, CII, TDRA Dubai, and the Government of Saudi Arabia, he blends research depth with competitive innovation. His YouTube channel has 55,000 subscribers covering AI, ML, Deep Learning, Cybersecurity, and Embedded Systems, and he holds a Limca Book of Records entry. He is an Intel oneAPI Certified Instructor, Goog
title: AI took my excuses, not my ideas | Shriram K Vasudevan | TEDxKIT Coimbatore

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if no poor child in India had to suffer from Type 1 diabetes? Dr Krishnan Swaminathan shares how his trust has given free care to over 4,300 children in nine years, and the 10-79-11 formula he believes can build a prosperous India. Dr Krishnan Swaminathan is a Consultant Endocrinologist at Idhayangal Charitable Trust, Coimbatore. He graduated from Madras Medical College and trained in Diabetes & Endocrinology across leading UK centres. His qualifications include MD (UK), FRCP from the Royal College of Physicians Edinburgh, and a PhD from IIT Madras on agrochemicals and diabetes.
As Managing Trustee of Idhayangal Charitable Trust, he supports 2000 poor children with Type 1 diabetes across India with analogue insulins, glucometers, strips, and 24/7 care. Idhayangal runs Asia's largest insulin pump programme for the underprivileged, with nearly 250 pumps. It also supports higher education for underprivileged girls with Type 1 diabetes and runs Project Sakthi to rehabilitate their mo
title: 10-79-11 formula for a prosperous India | Dr. Krishnan Swaminathan | TEDxKIT Coimbatore

author: TEDx Talks
description: Vania Celorio, atleta de alto rendimiento en taekwondo desde los tres años, la ponente relata su trayectoria desde convertirse en campeona nacional y quinta del mundo, hasta enfrentar las duras realidades fuera del podio: decisiones administrativas injustas, lesiones quirúrgicas y el desgaste emocional. A través de una profunda reflexión personal, explica cómo aprendió a dejar de definirse únicamente por sus medallas para abrazar un crecimiento integral, cultivando su mente, sus relaciones y el amor propio como la verdadera base del éxito dentro y fuera de la competencia. Vania Judith Celorio Lazcano es atleta mexicana de taekwondo nacida en Oaxaca, destacada en categorías juveniles y adulta. Ha ganado medallas en nacionales como la Olimpiada Nacional y representado a México en eventos CONADE y selectivos internacionales, posicionándose como promesa del deporte con logros en combate y formas. Su trayectoria inspira por superar retos desde joven en un deporte exigente, lo que la hace i
title: Resiliencia dentro y fuera del deporte | Vania Celorio | TEDxTecDeMty

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the next world-changing idea does not fail because it lacks potential — but because it lacks support? In this inspiring talk, the speaker explores the power of crowdfunding as a tool that allows ordinary people to turn meaningful ideas into reality. From startups and creative projects to humanitarian causes and social innovation, crowdfunding has transformed the way individuals and communities can support change together. The talk highlights how even small contributions, when combined through the power of community, can create opportunities that once seemed impossible. More importantly, it challenges the traditional belief that only large corporations, investors, or governments can drive impact. Through real examples and powerful insights, the speaker explains how crowdfunding is not only about raising money — it is about building trust, connecting people around a shared vision, and giving voices and ideas a chance to be heard. Ultimately, this talk is a reminder that collecti
title: Crowdfunding | Ruhshona A'zamjonova | TEDxNewUU

author: TEDx Talks
description: Quantum computing is no longer just a futuristic theory discussed by physicists — it is becoming a technology that could fundamentally reshape the modern world. In this fascinating talk, Fyodor Amanov introduces the audience to the principles behind quantum computing, exploring concepts such as quantum mechanics, superposition, and entanglement in a simple and engaging way. The talk explains how quantum computers differ from traditional computers and why their extraordinary processing power could revolutionize industries ranging from medicine and artificial intelligence to cybersecurity and scientific research. But beyond the science itself, the talk focuses on a deeper question: why should ordinary people care? As technology develops faster than society can fully understand it, quantum computing may influence the future of privacy, digital security, innovation, and even global power structures. The speaker encourages the audience not to fear complex technologies, but to become aware
title: Quantum Computing and Why You Might Need to Care | Fyodor Amanov | TEDxNewUU

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if waiting to feel “ready” is the very thing stopping people from creating meaningful change? In this powerful and deeply personal talk, Kamilla Beknazarova shares her journey from building her first technology initiative at the age of eleven to leading international projects in artificial intelligence, digital safety, education, and social innovation. Through the story of founding KB Lab and developing impactful systems such as environmental monitoring platforms, healthcare solutions, and cybersecurity initiatives for young people, she reflects on what it truly means to grow through uncertainty. The talk explores a challenge many young people face: feeling too inexperienced, too uncertain, or too unqualified to begin. Kamilla challenges the idea that confidence must come before action, showing instead that readiness is built through experimentation, failure, persistence, and courage. Drawing from experiences in global organizations, youth diplomacy, and technology leadership, sh
title: Starting Before You’re Ready: Building Impact Through STEM | Kamilla Beknazarova | TEDxNewUU

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the biggest limitation in life is deciding too early who we are supposed to be? In this inspiring talk, the speaker explores why people should never confine themselves to a single path, identity, or dream. By trying new experiences, exploring different interests, and stepping outside familiar environments, individuals gain a deeper understanding of themselves, their passions, and their purpose in life. Drawing from examples such as applying to universities abroad, participating in extracurricular activities, and exploring diverse academic subjects, the talk highlights how experimentation and curiosity help young people discover opportunities they never imagined for themselves. The speaker also emphasizes the importance of traveling and experiencing different cultures as a powerful way to broaden perspectives and better understand the world. Through competitions, exchange programs, leadership opportunities, and active involvement in communities, young people can challenge thems
title: Explore Yourself and the World | Dilafruz Sobirova | TEDxNewUU

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens when the dreams we carry for ourselves are shaped by the expectations of others? In this talk, Muhammad Zeeshan Mirza shares a deeply personal story about wanting to become a fiction writer, while being guided toward a more stable academic path that eventually led him to complete a PhD. Rather than focusing on regret or failure, the talk explores how decisions are often influenced by family, culture, responsibility, and collective values. Drawing from experiences common across many Asian societies, the speaker reflects on the difference between individual and collective decision-making — and why one should not be seen as superior to the other. This talk invites the audience to rethink what it means to choose a path in life, and reminds us that there is no single “correct” way to make decisions. What truly matters is the understanding, courage, and responsibility behind them. Dr. Muhammad Zeeshan Mirza is an Assistant Professor of Management at New Uzbekistan University. H
title: The story I wasn't allowed to write - and why that matters  | Dr. Muhammad Zeeshan Mirza | TEDxNewUU

author: TEDx Talks
description: Empathy is often seen as one of the most important human qualities — especially in education. But where is the line between supporting someone and lowering expectations for them? In this thought-provoking talk, Iroda Gulamova explores the growing tension between empathy, mental health awareness, and accountability in modern classrooms. Through personal stories, research, and real educational experiences, she examines how educators today face a difficult paradox: students need more understanding than ever before, yet excessive accommodation can unintentionally limit growth and resilience. The talk challenges the audience to rethink what true empathy means. Is being empathetic always fair? Or does real support sometimes require believing in someone’s potential enough to challenge them? Blending emotion, data, and powerful reflection, this talk offers a fresh perspective on education, expectations, and the responsibility we have toward one another. Irodakhon Gulamova is an Senior Lecture
title: Is it Fair to Be Empathetic? | Irodakhon Gulamova | TEDxNewUU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Every major global crisis feels like a problem that only governments, massive corporations, or specialized experts are meant to solve. But what if the most powerful solutions to our planet's greatest challenges are already sitting in our recycling bins and in the hands of everyday youth? 

This inspiring talk explores the story behind Liter of Light, a grassroots movement that transformed plastic bottles and basic electronics into zero-carbon, hand-built solar lighting for over a million people across 32 countries. 

It delivers a bold challenge to the next generation to stop waiting for permission to change the world. By harnessing creativity and radical resourcefulness, the youth around the world can stop being passive observers of global problems and start building a brighter, more sustainable future right in their own backyards.  Illac Diaz is an urban planner and social entrepreneur dedicated to empowering communities in the Philippines and globally through sustainable developmen
title: Why the Next Energy Revolution Belongs in Your Hands  | Illac Diaz | TEDxCISM Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
[EN] What would we be willing to tell a stranger about ourselves? As the photographer behind the viral Model Strangers account, Christopher approaches people on the street, photographs them and asks about their lives. The stories he uncovers are strikingly honest and deep.

[SK] Čo sme o sebe ochotní povedať cudziemu človeku pri náhodnom stretnutí?
Christopher ako fotograf z virálneho účtu Model Strangers oslovuje ľudí na ulici, fotí ich a pýta sa na ich život. Ich výpovede prekvapujú svojou úprimnosťou a hĺbkou.
 [SK] Christopher Ward, fotograf a rozprávač príbehov zo Severného Írska, oslovuje na ulici úplne neznámych ľudí a kladie im otázky, ktoré by sme možno nemali odvahu položiť ani vlastným priateľom.
V projekte Model Strangers z týchto stretnutí vznikajú úprimné portréty a rozhovory o túžbach, radostiach, ľútosti či smútku. Z krátkeho stretnutia cudzích ľudí sa stáva moment dôvery.
Milióny sledujú tieto príbehy online, možno preto, že v nich spoznávajú aj seba.

[EN] Christophe
title: Touched by splendid strangers, one portrait at a time | Christopher Ward | TEDxBratislava

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"Here is what I want to challenge". When most businesses hear “circularity”, they think recycling. But from a circularity perspective, recycling sits near the bottom — the last resort, once a product has already lost most of its value. It is one of the least circular things a business can do. We have mistaken the emergency exit — let's recycle our way out of this mess — for fixing a system that accepts waste in the first place.
So: does circularity make business sense in South Africa? We keep asking yes or no. I think that's the wrong question — and by the end I want to show you why the answer is neither.

The more you become a circular economy expert, the more the concept of circularity becomes fluffy — because you start to see systems, not just a linear line that moulds resources into products that eventually get discarded: the so-called linear economy.
 Katharina Gihring is a circular economy strategist and CEO of the African Circular Economy Network, where she works to turn circul
title: What ants taught me about business value | Katharina Gihring | TEDxUniversity of Johannesburg

author: TEDx Talks
description: What does it truly mean for a system to work, and how do we know when it is making a difference? Drawing from his experience as a civil servant in a remote district of Maharashtra, the speaker shares how an AI-powered monitoring system helped uncover gaps in school meals that official records had failed to reveal. Through the story of malnourished schoolgirls, a simple banana, and a young man who found the courage to pursue opportunities beyond his hometown, he explores how visibility, accountability, and human initiative can transform lives. He introduces the “Banana Test”, a simple yet powerful way to distinguish between completed tasks and meaningful impact. Ultimately, he challenges us to look beyond reports and statistics and ask what tangible changes we can actually see in the lives of the people we serve. Shubham Gupta is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer. In his public-service career he has led work across municipal governance, rural development, and tribal admini
title: The Banana Test | Shubham Gupta | TEDxImperial SBMS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when artificial intelligence makes a company 20% more productive? Who actually benefits from that extra value?

As AI and emerging technologies reshape the global economy, we face a fundamental choice: will innovation concentrate wealth in the hands of a few, or create opportunities for everyone?

Drawing on her experience leading businesses and supporting social innovation, Marta del Castillo challenges traditional models of capitalism and explores how companies can generate profit while creating meaningful social and environmental impact.

Through real-world examples, from sharing profits with employees during a crisis to transforming industrial waste into new business opportunities, she demonstrates why doing good and doing good business don't have to be competing goals.

This talk introduces a powerful alternative to both dystopia and utopia: protopia, a future built through continuous, practical improvements.

Because the future isn't inevitable. It's something we de
title: How to do good by doing good business | Marta Del Castillo | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the voice telling you that you're not good enough was never yours to begin with?

We all know that inner voice. The one that makes us question our worth, doubt our abilities, and fear that no matter how hard we try, we will never be enough. But where does it really come from?

Through a deeply personal story and her perspective as a psychotherapist, Lucrezia Maria Marino explores how childhood experiences, family expectations, emotional neglect, and inherited beliefs can shape the way we see ourselves.

Using the powerful metaphor of parents digging wells inside their children, she reveals how even actions driven by love can leave deep emotional wounds, and how the voices we grow up hearing can eventually become our own inner critics.

This talk is an invitation to recognize those inherited voices, reconnect with our authentic selves, and begin breaking cycles of emotional pain passed down through generations.

Because sometimes, finding your own voice begins with realizing th
title: Quella voce che non è la tua | Lucrezia M. Marino | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, what does it truly mean to be human? And could laughter hold part of the answer?

From the absurdity of everyday mistakes to the most difficult moments of human suffering, Leonardo Spina explores the extraordinary power of humor and its role in our lives.

Through comedy, philosophical reflections, and moving stories from his experience with hospital clowning, this talk reveals how laughter can help us confront failure, overcome fear, build meaningful connections, and bring moments of joy even in the darkest circumstances.

More than entertainment, laughter becomes an act of empathy, a bridge between people, and a powerful expression of our shared humanity.

Because sometimes, the most human thing we can do is simply laugh together. Leonardo Spina is a writer, screenwriter, actor, trainer, and gelotologist (laughter therapist). After studying Political Science and Literature, he worked with Dario Fo and trained at the screenwr
title: Ridere per restare umani | Leonardo Spina | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the fear of failure is actually the fear of discovering what we're truly capable of?

For as long as she can remember, Emma Galeotti has been convinced of one thing: one day, she will fail. From consistently finishing last in sports competitions to holding herself back from opportunities she genuinely cares about, failure has always felt like an inevitable part of her future.

But what happens when expecting failure becomes the very reason we never give ourselves a real chance to succeed?

Through sharp humor, uncomfortable honesty, and deeply personal stories, Emma explores the hidden mechanisms of self-sabotage, the fear of judgment, and the strange comfort of never giving 100%.

Rather than offering a perfect success story or an easy solution, she invites us to question the excuses we create to protect ourselves from disappointment.

Because perhaps the real failure isn't losing. It's never finding out what could have happened if we had truly tried. Emma Galeotti is a conte
title: Un giorno io fallirò | Emma Galeotti | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the greatest failure of your life isn't being different, but spending your life trying to be like everyone else?

Born without arms and with one leg shorter than the other, Nadia Lauricella spent much of her life feeling like she wasn't enough. Surrounded by judgment and society's expectations of what it means to be "normal," she became determined to change herself, believing that only then could she feel beautiful, worthy, and free.

But the harder she tried to fit into a world that wasn't designed for her, the further she drifted from who she truly was.

Through a deeply personal and emotional journey, Nadia challenges conventional ideas of beauty, perfection, disability, and self-worth. She shares how a life-changing conversation helped her shift from trying to fix herself to embracing her uniqueness.

This talk is a powerful reflection on self-acceptance, the courage to ask for help, and the freedom that comes from letting go of society's expectations.

Because true freedo
title: Cercare di essere NORMALE? Il mio più grande FALLIMENTO | Nadia Lauricella | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if being a failure is simply part of becoming successful?

We spend much of our lives trying to make the right decisions, avoid mistakes, and reach our goals. But what if success isn't defined by the destination, but by the journey itself?

Drawing inspiration from the legendary journey of Ulysses and his own experiences as an entrepreneur, Patrick Hoffer challenges the way we perceive failure, success, and the choices that shape our lives.

Through personal reflections, entrepreneurial lessons, and a comparison between Mediterranean and American attitudes toward failure, he explores why even our worst decisions can become essential chapters in our personal growth.

Because every choice, every setback, and every unexpected turn contributes to who we become.

Perhaps the greatest success isn't reaching the destination, but learning to embrace the journey, failures and all. Patrick Hoffer is an entrepreneur who has lived and shared the world of coffee for more than thirty years.

H
title: Io sono un fallito! Io sono un fallito?  | Patrick Hoffer | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The era of rigid five-year business plans is over. Drawing on two decades of building and reinventing an enterprise through seismic market shifts, Srikanth Acharya explores how everyday experimentation helps us outrun our own expiry date. Along the way, he reveals a timeless three-part rhythm of creation, preservation, and renewal that shapes the way we build, adapt, and evolve.


TEDxKLH University Bowrampet Licensee & Organizer - Bobba Thambi Aashish

An engineer turned entrepreneur, he built his business journey through experimentation, resilience and a will
title: Outrun Your Expiry: The Experimentation Advantage | Srikanth Acharya | TEDxKLH University Bowrampet

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if your biggest failure turned out to be the best thing that ever happened to you?

At 23, Camilla Brossa was living what she believed to be her dream life in San Francisco, working in the technology industry and building a promising future. Then, unexpectedly, she lost her job. And just when she thought she had rebuilt everything, it happened again.

But the second time, something changed. Instead of asking how to get her old life back, she began questioning whether she had been following the right path all along.

Through personal experiences, psychological insights, and powerful reflections, this talk explores the four fears that keep us from taking risks: uncertainty, loss, inadequacy, and the judgment of others. It challenges our perception of failure and reveals how changing the meaning we assign to setbacks can transform our lives.

Because failure isn't always the end of the road. Sometimes, it's the unexpected beginning of a life more aligned with who we truly are.

What
title: Per fortuna ho fallito: perdendo tutto ho trovato la mia strada | Camilla Brossa | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the biggest obstacle to achieving our dreams isn't failure, but the belief that we don't deserve to dream in the first place?

As a little girl, Giulia was told by her father that she would never have the beautiful home she dreamed of. Those words stayed with her for years, shaping the way she saw herself and what she believed was possible.

Through a deeply personal and emotional story, this talk explores the "DNA of scarcity": the limiting beliefs we inherit, often unconsciously, from the people around us. It challenges the illusion of safety within our comfort zones and reveals how easily we abandon our ambitions in the name of being realistic.

But dreaming big isn't just about believing. It's about taking responsibility, making sacrifices, and turning ambition into action.

Because sometimes, the greatest failure isn't falling short of our dreams. It's giving up on them before we even try. Giulia Fiorenza is an entrepreneur, educator, and founder of Booster Academy, where
title: Come tornare a sognare in grande | Giulia Fiorenza | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the biggest limits in our lives aren't the ones we have, but the ones others place on us?

For years, Andrea believed that loving and protecting his brother Giovanni, who has Down syndrome, meant shielding him from difficulties, disappointment, and failure.

But an unexpected lesson during a challenging Hyrox competition changed everything.

Through humor, vulnerability, and a powerful story of brotherhood, Andrea and Giovanni challenge the way we perceive disability, question the difference between protection and control, and reveal how even our best intentions can unintentionally limit the people we love.

Because true love isn't about protecting someone from every possible failure. It's about standing beside them while giving them the freedom to try, make mistakes, and discover their own potential.

The greatest failure isn't falling. It's denying someone the chance to try. Giovanni and Andrea Cerullo, known online as Gio&Andre, are brothers and content creators who share t
title: Che sei pazzo | Gio e Andre  | TEDxMarsala

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most of us measure health by a pulse and a prescription, ignoring the silent fractures in how we connect, reflect, and exist.

In Are You Really Alive? Realms of Awakening, Dr. Vikrant Singh Thakur challenges our narrow definition of well-being, guiding the audience through the physical, social, and spiritual dimensions of life.

Through deep self-reflection and self-discovery, he reveals how true metamorphosis begins the moment we stop merely surviving and awaken every realm of who we are.

With sincere gratitude to our Principal, university management, faculty coordinators, core organizing team, student volunteers, and everyone who supported us in bringing this event to life. Your guidance, dedication, and encouragement made this journey possible.

TEDxKLH University Bowrampet Licensee & Organizer - Bobba Thambi Aashish

 Dr. Vikrant Singh Thakur is an MD, DM Neurology specialist and the founder of TIME Neurocare in Karimnagar, Telangana. Dedicated to advancing neurological care, he
title: Are You Really Alive? Realms of Awakening | Vikrant Singh Thakur | TEDxKLH University Bowrampet

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if healing from grief isn't about moving on, but learning how to move forward with what we've lost?

Funeral director Shannan Guillory has spent years helping families navigate some of life's most difficult moments. But when her fiancé died unexpectedly just weeks before their wedding, she found herself facing the very grief she had spent her career helping others understand.

Drawing from her personal experience, Shannan offers an unexpected perspective on grief through the life of a snail. Using three simple principles — Carry, Retreat, Return — she challenges the idea that grief follows a timeline or that healing means returning to who we were before loss.

Her message invites us to rethink how we experience grief and, just as importantly, how we support those living with it. Because grief isn't something we have to overcome alone. It's something we can learn to carry together. Shannan Guillory is a licensed funeral director, grief advocate, and founder of Prism Memorial, dedi
title: The Snail Is a Grief Expert | Shannan Guillory | TEDxInglewood
